MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  JUNE 4, 2018

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
CHAIRMAN MEDAWAR.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Chair Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Edler, Scott, Yoo

  Commissioners Absent:  Schachter

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Sr. Planner Naughton,
  Administrative Assistant Corea

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING OF
  MAY 7, 2018.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL RESOLUTIONS THAT ARE PRESENTED FOR THE
  CONSIDERATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON TONIGHT’S AGENDA AND
  ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  B. CODE ENFORCEMENT SEMI-ANNUAL REPORT, DECEMBER 1, 2017 – JUNE 1, 2018

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by VICE CHAIR ZIGRANG to,

  APPROVE ITEMS 6-A AND 6-B

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

Items taken out of order

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 19-15; APPLICANT: TOLL BROTHERS; LOCATION:
  THE RESIDENCES AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB; A request to revisit two
  architectural designs – Modern Farmhouse Plans 1C and 4C – that were excluded from
  the approval of the architectural styles for 31 proposed homes in the Residences at Rolling
  Hills Country Club for development.

  Sr. Planner Naughton provided a PowerPoint presentation for this item.

  Planning Director Wahba added that the decision on this item will be included with the
  decisions made at the last planning commission meeting and presented to the City Council
  as one package at their next meeting on June 12, 2018.

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  approve the amendment to PA-19-15 to incorporate the proposed architectural styles of
  Plans 1C and 4C for the respective 31 lots.

  1
Planning Commission Minutes
June 4, 2018
   COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER EDLER to:

  APPROVE THE AMENDMENT AS RECOMMENDED BY STAFF.

  Ayes:  CHAIR MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, CARMAN, EDLER, SCOTT, YOO
  Noes:
  Absent:  SCHACHTER
  Abstain:

  A. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 06-18; APPLICANT: MR. PATRICK POPA; LOCATION:
  42 RANCHVIEW ROAD; A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for a
  first and second story addition to an existing single-story home. A Minor Deviation is
  required to decrease the front yard area by no more than 10%.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a PowerPoint presentation for this item and stated that
  staff has been working with this applicant on including the unpermitted structures on the
  property to either be demolished or brought up to compliance. The project will also include
  retaining walls and a future accessory dwelling unit, which are not shown on these plans,
  and will only require an administrative approval.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  approve PA-06-18 with the conditions as stated in the staff report.

  In response to a question by CHAIR MEDAWAR, Planning Director Wahba stated that the
  house and garage will have the same roof and the same paint color and this will be clarified
  as part of the conditions for approval.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the lot width is typical for Ranchview.  Planning
  Director Wahba stated that the narrow lot width is typical.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the minimum side setback requirement for a
  horsekeeping area. Planning Director Wahba stated that for developed lots, the
  horsekeeping area can be at the property line.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about the side setback for the “casita” drawn on the
  plans. Planning Director Wahba stated that this will need to be further explored.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he believes the horsekeeping area encroaches on
  a public trail and drainage ditch. Planning Director Wahba stated this will also need to be
  further explored.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed concerns with the height of the bathroom under the
  staircase and asked that it be checked. Planning Director stated that he believes the
  minimum height is 7 ft.

  In response to a question by VICE CHAIR ZIGRANG, Teresa Mendoza, Designer, stated
  that one palm tree will be taken out due to it being in the way of the new foyer.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Ms. Mendoza stated that she
  believes the bathroom height is 6’8” but will check if it meets the minimum requirements.

  Rich Olbroys, 40 Ranchview, expressed concerns about privacy since the proposed
  balcony is close to their home, and their home is at a lower grade. He is also concerned
  with the size and location of some of the windows. Lastly, Mr. Olbroys expressed concerns
  with the size and location of the proposed balcony.

  George Popa, 42 Ranchview, stated that the staircase to the balcony is on the opposite
  side of Mr. Olbroys property and added that the balcony has already been reduced by 7-
  8 ft. Mr. Popa stated that the windows could be changed to satisfy Mr. Olbroys concerns.

  VICE CHAIR ZIGRANG stated that in bedroom #4, the window looks low. Ms. Mendoza
  stated that the window is incorrectly shown on the plans to be low, but it will be at least 5
  ft. from the floor.

  VICE CHAIR ZIGRANG suggested a privacy screen on the side of the balcony that faces
  Mr. Olbry’s property. Ms. Mendoza agreed that this can be done.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated his concern with the size of the balcony but agreed that
  the privacy screen is a solution.

  2
Planning Commission Minutes
June 4, 2018
   Ms. Mendoza requested that the window in bedroom #3 be brought closer toward the front
  corner of the house in order to take advantage of the view. The Planning Commissioners
  agreed, but recommended that it be reduced to 4 ft. wide Mr. Popa also agreed.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION PA-06-18 WITH THE FOLLOWING
  MODIFICATIONS:
  1.  BEDROOM #3 WINDOW BE NO MORE THAN 4 FT. WIDE AND THAT
  IT BE LOCATED TO THE FRONT OF THE ROOM TO THE STAFF’S
  SATISFACTION;
  2.  THE BATHROOM GLASS TO BE OBSCURE.
  3.  THE WINDOW IN BEDROOM #4 TO BE A TRANSOM WINDOW WITH
  AT LEAST 5 FT. FROM THE FLOOR.
  4.  THE EASTERN PORTION OF THE BALCONY BE BUILT WITH A
  MINIMUM 6 FT. PRIVACY SCREEN.
  THIS WILL BE IN ADDITION TO STAFF’S EXISTING CONDITIONS.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG to:

  APPROVE THE AMENDMENT AS RECOMMENDED BY STAFF.

  Ayes:  CHAIR MEDAWAR, ZIGRANG, CARMAN, EDLER, SCOTT, YOO
  Noes:
  Absent:  SCHACHTER
  Abstain:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that years ago the regulations on outdoor rooms was
  discussed, in particular covered spaces on the first or second floors. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that this has been the compromise to not allowing rooftop decks, but
  understands the concern. COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that there will always be a
  privacy issue with second floor additions.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  Planning Director Wahba stated that the next meeting will be on July 2nd. Please notify
  staff if you will not attend.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, MAY 21, 2018.

  B. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, MAY 22, 2018.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11-A AND 11-B.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 8:03 p.m.

  __________________________

  Minutes Secretary  City Clerk
